content: This foam mattress arrived compressed in a box, but unboxing it felt like wrestling a stubborn octopus—it took nearly 45 minutes to fully expand and still had deep creases after 72 hours. The advertised “pressure-relieving memory foam” turned out to be overly dense and unyielding, making it feel less like sleeping on clouds and more like resting on a slightly warmed concrete slab. Within a week, I developed persistent lower-back stiffness—not the gentle support promised, but a dull, nagging ache that worsened each morning. The cover fabric is cheap, thin polyester that pills easily and traps heat like a sauna blanket, turning restless summer nights into sweaty ordeals. It also emits a strong, chemically sweet odor—like new carpet and burnt plastic—that lingered for over two weeks despite airing it in open windows and using fans. Edge support is virtually nonexistent: sitting or sleeping near the perimeter causes immediate, alarming sagging, making it unsafe and awkward to get in and out of bed. After just two months, visible body impressions over two inches deep have formed where I sleep, and the foam shows no sign of rebounding. Worst of all, customer service refused a full refund, offering only a 15% store credit—and only after I threatened to escalate to the BBB.
